question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a diagnostic thoracentesis?

options.A: To permanently seal the pleural space shut
options.B: To collect pleural fluid for laboratory analysis
options.C: To measure continuous pulmonary artery pressure
options.D: To deliver aerosolized antibiotics into the lungs

explanation: Diagnostic thoracentesis involves drawing a small fluid sample to identify the underlying cause of an effusion, such as infection or cancer. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h1)

question: A patient is struggling to breathe because of a massive buildup of fluid in the chest. Which type of procedure is needed?
explanation: Removing a large volume of fluid relieves lung compression and restores normal breathing capacity, which defines therapeutic intervention. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h1)

question: Where should the needle be placed when performing a thoracentesis?

options.B: Through the center of the sternum

explanation: Neurovascular bundles run along the lower edge of ribs, so insertion must occur over the upper border of the lower rib to prevent bleeding. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h2)

question: Why do healthcare providers usually drain pleural fluid from the back part of the chest?

options.A: The diaphragm sits higher on the anterior side
options.B: The chest wall is thinnest near the clavicle
options.C: Fluid naturally accumulates in the dependent posterior bases
options.D: Intercostal blood vessels are completely absent posteriorly

explanation: Gravity causes free-flowing pleural fluid to pool in the lower back regions of a patient who is sitting up. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the best position for a patient getting a thoracentesis?

options.B: Lying flat on the unaffected side
options.C: Flat on the back with arms extended
options.D: Prone with a pillow under the chest

explanation: Leaning forward spreads the ribs apart and moves abdominal organs away from the needle path. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h3)

question: Which lab test is most important for a nurse to check before a thoracentesis?

options.A: Coagulation studies like platelets and INR
options.B: Total serum protein and albumin values
options.D: Fast blood glucose and HbA1c levels

explanation: Normal clotting times and adequate platelets prevent excessive bleeding into the chest cavity during the needle puncture. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h3)

question: What should the nurse tell the patient to do while the needle is inside the chest?

options.C: Talk loudly to report chest pain

explanation: Sudden body movements or coughing can cause the lung tissue to hit the needle tip, increasing the risk of accidental lung puncture. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h4)

question: A patient suddenly turns pale, starts sweating, and feels dizzy during a thoracentesis. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Quickly withdraw more fluid to lower pressure
options.B: Increase the rate of intravenous fluids
options.C: Ask the patient to lie flat on the floor
options.D: Stop the procedure and notify the clinician

explanation: Sudden distress or a vasovagal reaction means the procedure must be paused or stopped immediately for safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h4)

question: What test is routinely ordered right after a thoracentesis is finished?
explanation: A chest X-ray checks that the lung has expanded properly and rules out a collapsed lung. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h5)

question: How should a patient be positioned right after the thoracentesis is complete?

options.A: Upright in a chair with arms raised overhead
options.B: Flat on the abdomen with head turned aside
options.C: On the unaffected side for a short duration
options.D: In a strict Trendelenburg position for two hours

explanation: Lying on the good side helps seal the puncture site on the treated side and encourages full lung expansion. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h5)

question: Which sign points to re-expansion pulmonary edema after fluid is removed from the chest?

options.A: Sudden sharp pain in the lower abdomen
options.B: Inability to move the lower extremities
options.C: Frothy pink sputum and severe cough
options.D: High fever with generalized skin rash

explanation: When a collapsed lung expands too quickly, fluid can leak into the tiny air sacs, causing a heavy cough and frothy pink sputum. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h6)

question: Which finding after a thoracentesis suggests a collapsed lung that needs urgent attention?

options.A: Stable blood pressure and normal heart rate
options.B: Absent breath sounds on the affected side
options.C: Mild soreness around the sterile bandage

explanation: Air leaking into the pleural space pushes the lung away from the chest wall, leading to muffled or totally absent breath sounds on that side. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h6)
